title: Greenworks’ MaximusZ electric riding mower has five motors and a few compromises
summary:
The 80-volt architecture within the MaximusZ mower here is the company’s latest, with Greenworks offering various packs of various sizes.
With a maximum speed of 8mph and 41 horsepower on tap, it’s comparable to something like a Stihl RZ 552, which retails for $9,499.
Squint, though, and you can see the current state of charge, maximum mower speed, maximum blade speed, and total runtime.
I fear the extra charging cycles these smaller packs face mean they’ll wear out more quickly than if the larger packs were depleted first.
Greenworks markets the MaximusZ as something that not only replaces a high-end zero-turn mower, but also serves as a mini utility vehicle around your property.

title: Agency says Hamsterley Forest campsite could 'risk life'
summary:
Plans for a campsite in a forest pose a "risk to life" and could pollute waterways, the Environment Agency (EA) has said.
Forestry England and Forest Holidays want to build 70 cabins, a campsite, cafe, restaurant, shop and staff accommodation in Hamsterley Forest, County Durham.
Routes out of the campsite would be forest tracks crossing or next to watercourses which might themselves be dangerous in the event of heavy rain, the agency added.
It recommended the whole campsite be relocated to an area with less flood risk, saying otherwise there would be a "risk to life and property" and a "danger for all people".
The use of a non-mains foul water drainage system could also pose an "unacceptable risk of pollution", the agency said.

title: Newsom returns to a defining California fight: Who pays for wildfire damage?
summary:
The most destructive wildfire in state history, a blaze that killed 85 people and destroyed more than 18,000 buildings in Northern California, started two days after Newsom won the governorship in 2018.
Months later, Newsom signed a law creating a $21 billion fund, paid for by utility shareholders and ratepayers, to help utilities pay for wildfire damages if they take certain safety measures.
Utilities have raised rates to pay for wildfire prevention and recovery as climate change has made the blazes more intense and frequent.
Newsom says the state needs to act quickly because he expects the wildfire fund to run out soon.
The California Professional Firefighters sent a letter to Newsom on Monday expressing its support for his proposal.

title: How “thunderquakes” could help reveal hidden structures inside the Earth
summary:
When that energy reaches the ground, some of it is converted into seismic waves that ripple through the soil and rock beneath.
The most important of these seismic waves are what we call air-coupled Rayleigh waves.
Thunderstorms offer a naturally occurring source of seismic energy that is already spread across the landscape.
Our thunderquake study revealed four distinct areas where seismic waves traveled much more slowly than through the surrounding rock.
Back on Earth, the atmosphere is constantly interacting with the ground beneath our feet.

title: Earth’s oceans just hit their hottest temperature ever recorded
summary:
Earth’s oceans just hit their hottest temperature ever—it’s only going to get worseAverage ocean temperatures hit a record 21.10 degrees Celsius (69.98 degrees Fahrenheit) on August 22, according to the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S).
That’s not as hot as a warm bath, but it is the hottest the world’s oceans have been since C3S started keeping records in 1979.
“As a climate scientist, this is not surprising to me all,” says Zachary Labe, a climate scientist at Climate Central, a climate research nonprofit.
The previous high, with a temperature of 21.09 degrees C (69.96 degrees F), occurred in March 2024, C3S said in a statement.
This cyclic climate pattern is marked by unusually hot Pacific Ocean temperatures, which can affect the entire planet’s weather.
